cards.heading: dollars on the blockchain
cards.body: A stablecoin is a cryptocurrency designed to maintain a stable value — usually pegged 1:1 to the US dollar. They bridge traditional finance and DeFi, letting you hold dollar value without leaving the blockchain.

cards.heading: why stablecoins matter
cards.body: Crypto prices swing wildly, but you still need a stable unit of account. Stablecoins let you park profits, pay for things, earn yield, and move money globally — all without touching a bank.

cards.text: Stablecoins process over $10 trillion in annual volume — more than Visa and Mastercard combined.

left.label: Fiat-backed (USDC, USDT)
items: backed by real dollars in bank accounts

cards.heading: algorithmic stablecoins
cards.body: Some stablecoins tried to maintain their peg using algorithms instead of real reserves. UST (Terra) was the most famous — it collapsed in May 2022, erasing $40B. The lesson: without real backing, pegs can break catastrophically.

cards.text: USDC is the most used stablecoin on Base. It's natively issued, meaning it's not bridged — fewer smart contract risks.

cards.heading: the redemption mechanism
cards.body: For USDC: anyone can deposit $1 with Circle and receive 1 USDC, or return 1 USDC and get $1 back. This creates a floor and ceiling — if USDC trades at $0.99, arbitrageurs buy it cheap and redeem for $1, pushing the price back up.

cards.heading: reserves and audits
cards.body: Fiat-backed stablecoins publish reserve reports showing they hold enough dollars (or short-term treasuries) to back every token. Circle publishes monthly attestations for USDC. Tether's reserves have been more controversial.

cards.text: Arbitrage is the invisible hand that keeps stablecoins at $1. When the price dips, traders profit by buying cheap and redeeming at par.

cards.heading: depeg events
cards.body: In March 2023, USDC briefly dropped to $0.87 after Silicon Valley Bank (which held $3.3B of Circle's reserves) collapsed. The peg recovered within days when the US government backstopped depositors.

cards.heading: signs of trouble
cards.body: Watch for: reserve composition changes, redemption delays, large deviations lasting more than hours, issuer legal troubles. A healthy stablecoin trades within ±0.5% of its peg virtually all the time.

cards.text: The UST death spiral: algorithmic peg broke → holders panic-sold → price dropped further → more selling. $40B gone in a week. Always check what backs your stablecoin.

cards.heading: native USDC on Base
cards.body: Base has native USDC — issued directly by Circle on Base L2, not bridged from Ethereum. This means lower risk, instant finality, and transfer fees under $0.001. It's the default stablecoin for Base DeFi.

cards.heading: what you can do with stablecoins on Base
cards.body: Lend for yield on Aave or Moonwell, provide liquidity on Aerodrome, swap between tokens, or simply hold dollar value while you research your next move. Gas costs are negligible.

cards.text: Sending $10,000 in USDC on Base costs less than a penny. The same transfer on Ethereum L1 could cost $5-20.
